What does an OS do?
* manage system resources
* provide an interface
==What is the OS approach==
Device e.g. mobile, PC, mainframe
User's perspective
==Von Neumann architecture==
Von Neumann built computers to have stored programs that are run from memory rather than the physical structure
==Powerup==
Program counter starts running itself when power supply starts
==Interrupts==
Interrupts are kind of like events, they are things that occur to operating systems at a hardware level that alert the CPU to make a change
==Dual mode- avoiding memory collissions==
Preventing collisions became a major thing

They introduced a mode bit 

# User Mode
# Kernel Mode
===System call===
Way that user processes get kernel mode permission

==Multiprocessor vs single processor==
Multiple processors means multiple processes can be run simultaneously but does not increase the speed of any given process
